newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwandan refugees quit Tanzanian camps.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees quit Tanzanian camps.

text.p: About 1,000 Rwandan refugees walked out of two camps in northwestern Tanzania on Sunday, complicating U.N. plans to repatriate them.

A spokesman for the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said half of the 1,000 refugees had gone off into the Tanzanian bush while the other half headed south, apparently intent on going home to Rwanda but skirting swampy land along the border.
They were from the camps of Kagenyi and Rubwera, which held about 38,600 Rwandans and were part of a chain of five camps in northwestern Tanzania, he added.

The spokesman, Peter Kessler, declined to speculate on the motives of the first group but aid workers in the Tanzanian town of Ngara said it was possible the refugees feared compulsory repatriation to Rwanda, where they or their relatives may face prosecution for the mass killings of minority Tutsis in 1994.

UNHCR and the Tanzanian authorities have given all 542,000 Rwandan refugees in Tanzania until the end of the month to go home. They take courage from the example of the Rwandans in Zaire, more than 600,000 of whom have gone home in one month.
The human rights organisation Amnesty International has criticised the plan as a form of forcible repatriation.

In Ngara, about 140 km (90 miles) south of the camps, Bradley Guerrant of the UN World Food Programme (WFP) suggested that Sunday's exodus was much bigger. "These two camps (Kagenyi and Rubwera) appear to be empty now," he said.
But Kessler said he had checked with UNHCR personnel on the ground and established that only 1,000 had left.
He said 300 other Rwandans were going on Sunday but most of those who have registered for repatriation wanted to wait for a food distribution on Tuesday before leaving.
On Friday and Saturday 4,700 refugees in the Tanzanian camps signed up for repatriation, he added.
